healthcareSystem: State-funded healthcare system with limited coverage for tourists. Public hospitals are underfunded. Private clinics in Bishkek offer better care. Most tourists pay out-of-pocket.
qualityNotes: Healthcare quality is limited, especially outside Bishkek. Private clinics in Bishkek provide acceptable care. Rural and mountain areas have very basic medical facilities. Serious conditions may require evacuation to Almaty or further.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies (аптека) generally open 8am-8pm weekdays. Some 24-hour pharmacies in Bishkek. Limited availability in rural areas.
pharmacyTips: Pharmacies are common in Bishkek and Osh but sparse in rural and mountain areas. Many medications available without prescription. Prices are low. Pharmacists rarely speak English. Stock up on essentials before trekking.
prescriptionRules: Prescription enforcement is lax. Many medications including antibiotics are available over the counter. Controlled substances such as opioids and benzodiazepines require a prescription.

restrictedMeds.name: Opioid medications
restrictedMeds.note: Strictly controlled. Carry a doctor's letter and original packaging.

restrictedMeds.name: Benzodiazepines
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled substance. Bring documentation from your doctor.

restrictedMeds.name: Pseudoephedrine-containing products
restrictedMeds.note: Restricted due to precursor drug controls.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter in English and Russian for any controlled medications. Keep all medications in original packaging with clear labels.

travelInsurance.tips: Strongly recommended, especially for trekking and adventure activities in remote mountain areas. Ensure your policy covers medical evacuation — helicopter rescue from mountain areas can be very expensive.

vaccinations.notes: No mandatory vaccinations. Ensure routine vaccinations are up to date. Rabies is present in rural areas.

waterNotes: Tap water is not reliably safe. Boil or treat water, especially outside Bishkek. Bottled water is cheap and widely available in towns. Mountain streams may appear clean but can harbor parasites.
foodSafetyTips: Stick to freshly cooked foods. Meat dishes like beshbarmak and laghman are generally safe when served hot. Be cautious with fermented mare's milk (kumis) if you have a sensitive stomach. Wash fruit and vegetables with clean water.
medicalTourismNote: Kyrgyzstan is not a medical tourism destination. For complex procedures, patients typically travel to Almaty (Kazakhstan), Istanbul, or Moscow.
metaDescription: Health guide for Kyrgyzstan: emergency numbers, pharmacy tips, restricted medications, vaccinations, water safety tips, and insurance advice.

hospitals.name: Bishkek Scientific Research Center of Traumatology and Orthopedics
hospitals.notes: Major public hospital for trauma cases. Limited English but handles emergencies.

hospitals.name: Neo Vita Clinic
hospitals.notes: Private clinic with modern equipment. Some English-speaking staff. Popular with expats.

hospitals.name: National Hospital (Bishkek)
hospitals.notes: Largest public hospital. Emergency department 24/7. Language barrier likely.

hospitals.name: Osh City Clinical Hospital
hospitals.notes: Main hospital in the south. Basic facilities. Russian and Kyrgyz spoken.

pharmacyPhrases.english: I need medicine for a headache

dentalCare.availability: Basic dental care available in Bishkek. Very limited outside the capital.
dentalCare.costRange: $10-30 for consultation; $20-60 for fillings; $15-40 for extractions
dentalCare.notes: Private dental clinics in Bishkek offer reasonable quality at low prices. Equipment may not be the latest.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: Seek private dental clinics in Bishkek for emergencies. In rural areas, dental care is extremely limited — carry a basic dental emergency kit for trekking trips.

mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Very limited. Some expat-oriented services in Bishkek.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are underdeveloped. English-speaking therapists are rare. Online therapy platforms may be the best option for travelers.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility infrastructure is very limited throughout Kyrgyzstan. Sidewalks are uneven, ramps are rare, and most buildings lack accessible features.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Major hospitals in Bishkek have ground-floor access but limited wheelchair accommodation. Rural facilities are not accessible.
accessibilityInfo.transport: Public transport is not wheelchair accessible. Taxis are the most practical option. Adventure tourism areas are largely inaccessible for mobility-impaired travelers.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Contact tour operators in advance about accessibility needs. Bishkek is relatively flat but sidewalks are in poor condition. Mountain destinations require good mobility.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.testing: COVID tests available at clinics in Bishkek.
covidStatus.notes: Kyrgyzstan has lifted all COVID-related entry restrictions.

insuranceClaimProcess: Private clinics can provide receipts and basic medical reports. Request documentation in English if possible. Keep all receipts — healthcare is inexpensive but documentation standards vary.

commonCosts.note: Estimated typical out-of-pocket costs at private or international facilities. Public-system rates can be much lower. Actual costs vary by city, facility, and exchange rate.

medicalEvacuation.note: Medical evacuation insurance is essential for mountain trekking. Helicopter evacuations from remote areas can cost $10,000+. Almaty is the nearest city with advanced medical facilities.
